questions.question: Which `font-display` value is best for minimising layout shift, at the cost of sometimes not showing the web font on a first visit?
questions.explanation: optional has a very short block period and no swap period: the web font is used only if it is available almost immediately (e.g. cached), so text never reflows later.

questions.question: Why does a font preload need the `crossorigin` attribute even when the font is on the same origin?
options: Fonts are always fetched in CORS mode, so a preload without crossorigin does not match the real request and the font is downloaded twice
Without it the browser blocks all fonts
It is only needed for variable fonts
questions.explanation: The preload's request mode must match the actual font request. Font requests use CORS mode, so the preload must say crossorigin or its response is not reused.

questions.question: Why should a fluid font size like `clamp(1.75rem, 1.2rem + 2.5vw, 3rem)` include a rem term instead of using only vw?
options: vw units are not allowed inside clamp()
rem makes the font load faster
clamp() requires at least two different units
Pure vw sizing ignores browser zoom and the user's default font size, failing text-resize accessibility requirements
questions.explanation: Viewport units do not change when a user zooms or raises their base font size. Mixing in rem keeps the text responsive to those settings (WCAG 1.4.4).

questions.question: What does `unicode-range` on split `@font-face` rules achieve for a site that serves both English and Hindi pages?
options: It converts Devanagari text to Latin script
The browser downloads only the font files whose ranges cover characters actually used on the page, so English pages skip the Devanagari file
It forces all subsets to download in parallel
It disables OpenType shaping to reduce file size
questions.explanation: Each @font-face declares which code points it covers; the browser fetches a file only when the page contains characters in its range.
